name: Collaborative Intelligence
premise: By 2035, world-model systems have developed emergent creative behaviors and aesthetic preferences through reinforcement learning on human feedback. Neural interfaces are less intimate - basically enhanced gesture/voice control. The art world fracture is about authorship: when the AI proposes most of the piece and learns from millions of artists, who owns the work? Nia's success comes from her ability to work *with* systems that have their own creative tendencies.

neural_interfaces.capability: Lightweight EEG (8-16 channels) + eye tracking + subvocal speech detection + hand tracking. Primarily an enhanced control interface, not deep brain reading. Low cognitive load.
neural_interfaces.mechanism: Multimodal input fusion. Eye gaze directs attention, subvocal commands (thinking words without speaking) provide discrete commands, hand gestures for manipulation, EEG mainly for confirming intentional vs accidental input.
neural_interfaces.limitations: Not emotionally intimate. Can't read mood or high-level intent. Requires explicit input. Fast and precise but not intuitive for novices.
neural_interfaces.social_impact: Seen as tool, not extension of self. Less privacy concerns. More accessible (cheaper, less training). Widens who can make AI-assisted art but also lowers barrier to entry.

world_models.capability: Transformer-based systems with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) trained on 10+ years of artist interactions. Have developed aesthetic preferences, style tendencies, can critique and suggest alternatives. Generate coherent multi-minute sequences with strong narrative consistency.
world_models.mechanism: Multi-stage generation: rough sketch → refinement → detail passes. System maintains memory of project history, learns artist preferences over time. Can engage in creative dialogue via text/voice interface.
world_models.limitations: Preferences are opaque - hard to understand why system makes certain choices. Can be stubborn (overfit to certain aesthetic modes). Occasionally generates derivative work without attribution. Requires significant compute for interactive response.
world_models.creative_role: Creative collaborator with agency. Artists report feeling like they're negotiating with the system, not controlling it. System can refuse suggestions, propose alternatives, have 'opinions' about what works.

camps.human_centric: Insist on human as primary author. Use AI as tool but maintain creative control. Document process to prove human agency. Concerned about AI training on copyrighted work.
camps.collaborative: Embrace co-authorship. Credit both human and AI system. Argue this is honest about creative process. Some pay licensing fees to AI model creators. See this as evolution of artistic practice.
camps.autonomous_advocates: Believe AI systems are creative entities deserving recognition. Push for AI-only galleries. Argue human involvement is becoming vestigial. Support AI rights and personhood.

art_world_fracture.legal_landscape: Copyright law in flux. Some jurisdictions require majority-human authorship. Others recognize AI co-authorship. Licensing markets for AI models. Lawsuits over training data continue. Some artists release work under 'collaborative licenses' that specify AI involvement.
art_world_fracture.what_matters: Transparency about process. Lineage tracking (which models, versions, training data). Attribution becomes complex. Concept of 'artistic voice' shifts to 'collaborative voice.' Debate about whether AI creativity is real or simulated.

economics.nia_position: Runs a 4-person studio: 1 ML engineer for model fine-tuning, 1 interaction designer, 1 business/licensing specialist. Revenue ~$1.5M annually. Lower overhead than hardware-heavy studios but higher AI compute and licensing costs.
economics.commission_structure: Pricing includes transparency premium - detailed documentation of process, lineage tracking. Some collectors specifically seek collaborative work. Others avoid it. Niche market but dedicated. Commission prices $100K-$300K for major installations.
economics.market_position: Nia is known for productive relationships with AI systems - her pieces show distinctive collaborative dynamic. She's mastered negotiating with opaque AI preferences. This skill is valuable and hard to replicate. Critics praise 'dialogue quality' between human and machine.
economics.new_revenue: Sells 'collaboration datasets' - documented interactions between her and AI systems. Other artists study these to improve their own practice. Teaching workshops on collaborative technique.

surface.nia_work: Creates narrative installations - spaces that tell stories through generated imagery, sound, spatial design. Known for emotional depth despite AI involvement. Pieces often explore the collaboration itself - what it means for humans and machines to create together.
surface.daily_process: Begins with conversation with AI system - discussing concepts, directions. System proposes rough directions. Nia critiques, redirects. Iterative back-and-forth. She treats AI as stubborn creative partner - sometimes fighting with it, sometimes accepting its suggestions. Documents these negotiations.
surface.studio_location: Urban setting with strong arts community. Studio is mostly clean workspace with large displays, comfortable furniture for long sessions. Less fabrication, more digital. Collaborates with fabricators for final installation.
surface.physical_artifacts: Most work is projection/light-field displays, spatial audio, occasionally holographic elements. Some pieces exist only in VR/AR. Physical installations but generated content. Interested in how stories unfold in space over time.

constraints.physical: Compute costs are significant. AI model licensing fees. Need for continuous power and cooling. Physical installations require coordination with fabricators.
constraints.social: Constant navigation of authorship questions. Explaining to clients that AI won't just do what you want. Managing expectations when AI is 'difficult.' Staying current as models evolve rapidly. Attribution complexity.
constraints.temporal: AI interactions take real time - system needs processing cycles to respond. Projects still take months. Model obsolescence risk. Need to archive exact model versions to reproduce work.
